clue.text: Price of 20 for itinerant healer, former pupil, going in from there and going on

definitions.note: the price per foot of maple, the timber at 20 across

indicators.note: the next pieces are said to go in, so they are placed inside the word for 'from there'

parts.note: thence means from that place

indicators.note: an itinerant wanders about, so the letters of healer wander into a new order

parts.note: FP is the Scottish abbreviation for former pupil, like the English 'old boy'
afoot means under way, happening

explanation.surface: A travelling quack and an old schoolboy set off from somewhere and keep walking, at some cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged healer letters and FP go inside the 'from there' word after its first two letters. Marriott Edgar's comic monologue 'Three Ha'pence a Foot' has Noah haggling with a timber merchant over maple for the Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: In the monologue the merchant's quoted rate for maple timber is this sum per running foot.

clue.text: Complete obliteration of story on pieces of film in digital envelope

indicators.note: the story and film pieces are placed in the envelope word

parts.note: a toe is a digit, here pictured as wrapping round the other letters

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a tale is a story
clips are short pieces of film

explanation.surface: A tale spliced from film clips gets wiped out inside some digital packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digital envelope' sounds like computing, but the digit is a toe, whose letters wrap round the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A total eclipse blots out the sun entirely, a complete obliteration of its light.

clue.text: Producer of red berries from Lambeth?

definitions.meaning: the mountain ash tree bears bright red berries
Lambeth Palace is the London home of the Archbishop of Canterbury, at the time Dr Williams, whose first name this is

explanation.surface: Where do the red berries come from: south London?
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash bears red berries, and Archbishop Williams of Lambeth Palace had this first name.

clue.text: Change of heart a drawback when descending?

indicators.note: a change of the word heart means its letters are altered in order

parts.note: read as 'draw back': the word draw written backwards

explanation.surface: Changing one's heart is a drawback when going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' must be split into 'draw' and 'back': the second half is the reversal signal for the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving earthward means heading towards the ground, which is what descending involves.

clue.text: One in 2 or 20, of course

parts.note: one is a, the indefinite article
the answers at 2 down and 20 across are both kinds of tree

explanation.surface: One horse among two or twenty runners, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but the course is the racecourse near Liverpool where the Grand National is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree is the racecourse near Liverpool that hosts the Grand National steeplechase.

clue.text: Sudden outbreak causing about turn in panic

indicators.note: the pieces for 'about turn' are placed in the panic word

parts.note: a flap is a state of panic
re means about or concerning
U is a turn, as in U-turn

explanation.surface: A sudden outbreak that makes someone do an about-turn in a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare-up is a sudden burst of trouble or illness, an outbreak.

clue.text: Succeed in removing it from private bathroom

indicators.note: removing signals that the letters of it come out of the bathroom word

parts.note: an en suite is a bathroom attached to a bedroom

explanation.surface: Getting on in life by taking the en suite out.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on afterwards, the sense of succeed as coming next.

clue.text: Cheat to go on and on after getting his notice?

indicators.note: the harping piece follows the notice piece

parts.note: to get one's cards is British for being dismissed from a job
to harp on is to talk about something repeatedly

explanation.surface: A worker given notice keeps complaining about it.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an employee who is sacked 'gets his cards', the documents handed back on leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardsharp cheats at card games for money, so he is a type of cheat.

clue.text: See 14
Number for a hospital on channel island saved us from 1 down, as it were

definitions.text: saved us from 1 down, as it were

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A hospital number allocated on Sark rescued us from a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The flood was a total obliteration of the world, so the vessel that preserved life saved us from it, 'as it were'.
explanation.definitionFit: The vessel in Genesis carried Noah's family and the animals through the Flood, preserving life on earth.

clue.text: Indecent books withdrawn (including most of Thackeray's) on a day in July

indicators.note: the shortened novel title is taken inside the other word
withdrawn says the letters for the books are taken out

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: most of says the title loses its tail

parts.note: Pendennis is a novel by William Makepeace Thackeray

explanation.surface: Smutty books get pulled from the shelves, Thackeray included, on a July holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' leaves INDECE; 'most of' leaves PENDEN, which goes inside after the first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Independence Day on the fourth of July is the American national holiday, so the word names that day.

clue.text: Abroad, the one expensive meal taker

parts.note: in French 'the one' is l'un
cher is French for expensive

explanation.surface: Abroad, one costly diner stands out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' tells you to work in French: l'un for 'the one' and cher for 'expensive'.
explanation.definitionFit: A luncher is someone eating lunch, literally one who takes a midday meal.

clue.text: The schemer's only part of the writer

indicators.note: part of signals that the answer lies within the run of words before

explanation.surface: The plotter is just a part of the author.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across schemer's and only.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American essayist and poet, a famous writer.

clue.text: Firm supporter of poisoner

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
a bra is an undergarment that supports

explanation.surface: A loyal backer of a poisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm supporter' reads as a staunch ally, but splits into firm and supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: The cobra is a venomous snake, so in crosswords it can be called a poisoner.

clue.text: Whale keeps changing tack around the water, high spot of holiday?

indicators.note: the whale word keeps the rest inside it

parts.note: a whale is called a blower because it spouts

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the water word
changing signals the letters of tack are reordered

parts.note: a pool is a body of water

explanation.surface: A whale keeps tacking around the water, the best bit of a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' gives ACKT, which goes around the water word; all that sits after the whale word's first two letters. The tower is the tall seaside landmark in the Lancashire resort of Blackpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackpool's tower is the tallest structure in that seaside resort, literally a high spot on holiday.

clue.text: Hold forth on right being taken away from resident alien

indicators.note: the letter for right is removed from the other word

parts.note: an expatriate lives in a foreign country

explanation.surface: Ranting about rights being stripped from a foreign resident.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at great length, which is to hold forth.

clue.text: Childish complaint of boat in loch being both unfinished

indicators.note: both the boat word and the loch word lose their final letters
the boat word is placed in the loch word

parts.note: Loch Tummel is a lake in Perthshire, Scotland
a yacht is a sailing boat

explanation.surface: A child grumbles about a boat on a Scottish loch.
explanation.walkthrough: Loch Tummel is in the Scottish Highlands; 'both unfinished' trims the last letter from each of the two words, so YACH ends up inside TUMME.
explanation.definitionFit: Tummy ache is the nursery term for stomach pain, a complaint typical of children.

clue.text: What can't be caught can be made bad in lieu

indicators.note: the letters can be made into something new, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: Something misheard can be made worse in place of something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like catching a cold or a ball, but means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound that cannot be heard, or caught, is inaudible.

clue.text: Better-looking and not so plump when disheartened

indicators.note: when links the thinner word to the condition, so the answer is that word with its missing heart restored

parts.note: bonier means more bony, thinner
the heart lost is the middle letter of the answer, which must be put back

explanation.surface: Prettier and slimmer when feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: take the heart (the middle N) out of the answer and you get BONIER, meaning thinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonny is Scots and northern English for pretty, so the comparative means prettier.

clue.text: Conclusion: mice sadly may well be ineradicable

parts.note: an end is a conclusion

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters of mice are in a bad state, reordered

explanation.surface: Final verdict: mice, unfortunately, may be impossible to get rid of.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic disease or pest is native and permanently present in an area, so likely hard to eliminate.

clue.text: Sam's corner — he keeps little money — wanted for 9

indicators.note: the he word keeps the coin letter inside it

parts.note: he denotes a male
p is a penny, a small amount of money

explanation.surface: Sam runs his corner shop on a shoestring, and his stock is wanted for a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: In the monologue, timber merchant Sam Oglethwaite has cornered the market in the wood Noah wants for the Ark (9 across).
explanation.definitionFit: Sam had cornered the supply of this hardwood timber, which Noah needed for his boat.

clue.text: Tenant from Peter-borough makes no mistake

indicators.note: a mistake jumbles things, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenant from Peterborough gets everything right.
explanation.walkthrough: The Soke of Peterborough was a historic district; a sokeman was a tenant holding land under the old soke system.
explanation.definitionFit: A sokeman was a medieval tenant holding land within a soke, a jurisdiction like the Soke of Peterborough.

clue.text: Wine is both your tormentor and therapist

parts.note: ME is myalgic encephalomyelitis, the illness that torments sufferers
doc is short for doctor

explanation.surface: A drink that both torments and heals you.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red wine region of Bordeaux, and its wines carry the name.

clue.text: Country under Prohibition only on top of 14 8 in 9's day

definitions.meaning: a place where alcohol is banned is called dry, so this is literally dry territory

definitions.text: only on top of 14 8 in 9's day
definitions.meaning: in the monologue the Flood covers all but the top of Blackpool Tower, the one patch not under water

explanation.surface: Under Prohibition, the only safe spot was atop the tower in Noah's time.
explanation.definitionFit: Land not under water is dry ground; in Noah's flood only the tower top stayed above it.

clue.text: See 1 across
My sword I wield to deal with noisy behaviour

indicators.note: wielding a sword swings it about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Brandishing a sword to deal with rowdiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdyism is unruly, boisterous conduct, the noisy behaviour of hooligans.

clue.text: Major mark of forty times 1 across

definitions.meaning: a royal ... is a principal emblem or mark of sovereignty
forty times one and a half old pence is sixty pence, five shillings, the value of this old British coin

explanation.surface: A big sign worth forty times the price.
explanation.walkthrough: Pre-decimal Britain had 12 pence to the shilling; a crown coin was worth five shillings, which is sixty old pence.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown is the chief symbol of monarchy, and also the old five-shilling coin.

clue.text: Boiler for some famous people backing deceptive alien outlet

indicators.note: backing signals the letters are written in reverse

parts.note: part of the word celebs
trick, as an adjective, means deceptive, like trick photography
ET is the film's extraterrestrial
read as 'let out': the letters of let rearranged

explanation.surface: A kettle for celebrities using a sly extraterrestrial power socket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the start of celebs into ELEC; 'outlet' is read as 'let out', an anagram signal giving TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle is a vessel that boils water, so it is fairly called a boiler.
